text: Not all decompositions of schemas are helpful. Consider an extreme case in which all schemas consist of one attribute. No interesting relationships of any kind could be expressed. Now consider a less extreme case where we choose to decompose the employee schema (Section 6.8): employee (ID, name, street, city, salary) into the following two schemas: employeel (ID, name) employee2 (name, street, city, salary) The flaw in this decomposition arises from the possibility that the enterprise has two employees with the same name.
